I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for a gravimetric, volumetric or flow H2 uptake value (wt%, mmol/g, isotherm). None found. Nearest: SI Fig. S16 plots residual headspace H2 concentration (uM), about 3000 for blank and every NG.

I5.quote: Vinyl chloride (VC) is a dominant carcinogenic residual in many aged chlorinated solvent plumes, and it remains a huge challenge to clean it up.

notes: Primary experimental paper on vinyl chloride reduction by nZVI amended with N-doped graphene (NG); not a review, not retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the text). I1 judged not met. The only H2 sorption test is SI Fig. S16 (si1, p. 21): '2 mL of pure H2 gas were added to sealed 10 ml vials containing 5 ml of 4 g/L of NG, and then equilibrated for 3 days under shaking, prior H2 analysis.' The plotted quantity is H2 concentration (uM) read on a reduction gas detector (SI Text S3), blank and NG400 to NG1100 all about 3000-3100 uM. Main text p. 8: 'The sorption of NG materials towards H2 was also tested, but no significant differences were observed between different NGs (Fig. S16)'. No uptake per sorbent mass is reported, the sorbent is suspended in water, and the method is a headspace GC check, not a gravimetric, volumetric or flow uptake measurement. The other hydrogen in the paper is H2 formed by nZVI corrosion (Fig. 6, umol H2 produced) and hypothesised atomic-H storage, neither an uptake from the gas phase. Not coded electrochemical: there is no electrode, applied potential or electrochemical charging. Sensitivity: if the Fig. S16 headspace test were read as a volumetric-type uptake measurement, I2 would be met (NG is 86.6-98.4 mass% C, SI Table S2) and I4 would be met (SI Text S1 gives a supplier surface area of 300 m2/g for the graphene nanoplatelets, product 900394; BET area of the NGs by N2 sorption, main Section 2.5, values in SI Fig. S5), but I3 would fail: no numeric temperature or pressure is stated for the H2 test (room temperature is stated only for the VC experiments, and no vial pressure is given anywhere). The code would then still be no_conditions_stated.
